svg.text: ShellA dome with a large door arch
The frame is a cut of the shell itself · set first, courses bear on it · from Nina’s sketch
A
Plinth (open at the door) + door frame set first
(blue, precast or anchored, 17 blocks)
B
Courses laid against the frame,
stapled as before (70 blocks)
C
Finished dome, staples out
D
Front view · arch 1.6 m wide, crown 1.25 m (was 0.95 m wide, 0.98 m high)
E · Door arch: what changed
Opening 1.6 m wide from the ground: straight jambs
to 0.45 m, round arch to 1.25 m (dome rise 1.65 m).
17 shell blocks near the opening are cut by one
plane (jamb or arch face) and become the frame.
14 blocks fall inside the opening and are left out.
The frame is set first and fixed to the plinth,
like a precast door ring; shell courses bear on it.
180 shell blocks remain, 438 staples.
The plinth ring and sill are cut away in the doorway:
6 pieces removed, 1 cut to the jamb, so the opening
reaches the ground — level entry.
Isaac Sim renders of the staple build with the enlarged arch · geometry: Report 04 ShellA at 0.6×, door frame cut from the shell blocks
